why: Quote is verbatim (plugins/host-marketplace.md#depend-on-and-recommend-other-plugins (was line 83 of the retired plugin-dependencies page)) and the cited docblock exists (claude.ts:1582-1589; the claim's 1576-1584 span is off by ~6 lines but lands in the same comment). The identifier facts are all accurate: `allowCrossMarketplaceDependenciesOn` has zero readers anywhere in packages/ or apps/ (grep -a: the only hits are the claude.ts:1583 comment, two plan docs and the deviation register), no `cross-marketplace` error code exists (grep -a for 'cross-marketplace|crossMarketplace' over all .ts returns one comment at plugins/types.ts:703), and `PluginDependencyDescriptor.marketplace` really is carried and consumed (dependencies.ts:91,99; management-service-v2.ts:711,714,748). The CONSEQUENCE is what fails, in the exact 'enforcement one layer up' shape AGENTS.md and inert-worklist section 4 item 3 warn about. The doc scopes the refusal to auto-install: ':81' reads 'Claude Code refuses to AUTO-INSTALL a dependency that lives in a different marketplace', and ':104' blesses the escape hatch 'Users can still install the dependency manually first, which satisfies the constraint without changing the allowlist.' Nessy auto-installs no plugin dependency at all -- verified one layer down: `resolvePluginDependencyErrors` (dependencies.ts:68-140) only resolves declared dependencies against ALREADY-INSTALLED subjects and emits dependency-unsatisfied / dependency-version-unsatisfied / range-conflict, and `resolveTransitiveDependencies` (management-service-v2.ts:696-728) throws `plugin.manage.dependency-not-installed` rather than fetching; nothing in the plugin install path resolves a dependency from a marketplace. So every cross-marketplace dependency Nessy can ever satisfy is one the user installed manually, which is precisely the path ':104' says satisfies the constraint WITHOUT the allowlist. The trust property the field protects -- 'This prevents one marketplace from silently pulling in plugins from a source you have not reviewed' -- is therefore satisfied strictly more conservatively than Claude, not violated. What differs is only the diagnostic string (dependency-unsatisfied / dependency-not-installed instead of a `cross-marketplace` error naming the field), not the security outcome. It is also an already-recorded deviation with a written reason, harvested by scripts/regenerate-deviation-register.py from docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-30-plugin-dependencies-and-monitors.md:243 into docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:392 (and an earlier one at 2026-07-29-marketplace-entry-authority.md:226). It is NOT one of the nine dated owner decisions in inert-worklist section 3 -- I checked all nine and none concerns marketplaces or dependencies -- so it is refuted as a false consequence plus a recorded deviation, not as a section-3 owner decision.
correctedState: Accurate as far as the identifiers go, but the divergence does not exist as a behaviour gap. `allowCrossMarketplaceDependenciesOn` has no reader in packages/ or apps/ and no `cross-marketplace` error code exists, yet plugins/host-marketplace.md#depend-on-and-recommend-other-plugins (was line 81 of the retired plugin-dependencies page) scopes the refusal to AUTO-INSTALL and :104 states that manually pre-installing the dependency satisfies the constraint without the allowlist. Nessy auto-installs no dependency on any path (dependencies.ts:68-140 resolves only against installed subjects; management-service-v2.ts:696-728 throws plugin.manage.dependency-not-installed rather than fetching), so manual pre-install is the only path that exists and every satisfied cross-marketplace dependency is doc-conformant by :104. The `marketplace` field is not merely parked for a future check -- it is live input today at dependencies.ts:99 and management-service-v2.ts:711/748, where it selects which marketplace a dependency resolves in. The only real delta is the diagnostic code (dependency-unsatisfied / dependency-not-installed rather than a `cross-marketplace` error naming the field to set). Recorded deviation: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-30-plugin-dependencies-and-monitors.md:243.
